stem: A 6-month-old infant is being evaluated for faltering growth; which associated symptom cluster most strongly suggests chronic anaemia as a contributing organic problem?

options.text: Feeding difficulties, hypersomnolence, and poor suck
Delayed puberty with delayed bone age
Height within 3 centiles of mid-parental height

explanation: Feeding difficulties, hypersomnolence, and poor suck are the symptom cluster that most strongly suggests chronic anaemia in an infant with faltering growth.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf p.104

optionExplanations.A: Correct because chronic anaemia in babies can present with feeding difficulties, hypersomnolence, and poor suck, and may contribute to faltering growth.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because frequent regurgitation with otherwise normal growth is more consistent with uncomplicated gastro-oesophageal reflux.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because delayed puberty with delayed bone age is more suggestive of constitutional delay than chronic anaemia.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because body disproportion suggests a skeletal dysplasia rather than anaemia.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a height within 3 centiles of mid-parental height supports familial short stature rather than anaemia.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
